title: dedicated-capacity-weekly-prep-scratchpad
content:
Context / purpose:
- Quick prep notes for weekly 1:1 with Samir (capacity owner) and sync with Emma (product) afterwards.
- Focus: next quarter reservations, short-term spike handling, and autoscale trigger tuning.

Top-line asks for meeting:
1) Confirm Q2 reservation target and margin (how many committed GPUs by region).
2) Decide on conservative burst buffer policy for unexpected enterprise spikes.
3) Review proposed change to autoscale thresholds (95% -> 90% for headroom).
4) Identify immediate follow-ups and owners + deadlines.

Data snapshot (quick numbers to cite) — current as of 2026-03-08 telemetry:
- Total dedicated GPUs (prod): 820 (us-west-2: 380, us-east-1: 260, eu-west-1: 180)
- Average 7d utilization (token-processing): 62% overall (p95 latency SLO currently met)
- Peak 24h spike yesterday: 91% sustained for 3 hours in us-west-2 (queueing observed)
- Reserved capacity (monthly commits): 600 GPUs (so ~220 are on pay-as-you-go/burst)
- Cost per GPU-hour (blended committed): $1.10; on-demand ~$2.90

Assumptions for Q2 forecast (starter model):
- Growth rate (served requests): +18% month-over-month for paid customers (based on usage cohort movement)
- Target utilization band: 55% - 75% (we aim to stay in this band for cost predictability)
- Minimum burst buffer: 12% of total capacity in region (we may adjust by SLA tier)

Preliminary recommendation (what I want us to agree on):
- Move to commit an additional 120 GPUs in us-west-2 for Q2 to cover growth + reduce on-demand spend.
- Keep eu-west-1 flat for Q2 but re-evaluate mid-quarter if growth > 12% m/m.
- Implement a regional burst pool (shared across tenants) limited to 60 GPUs for emergency spikes, billed to a central cost center.
- Lower the autoscale high-water threshold from 95% -> 90% to give 1–2 minutes of headroom for scaling ops (need perf validation).

Risks / open questions to raise:
- Does committing extra capacity lock us into a worse price if demand flattens? (finance input needed)
- How will burst pool interact with tenant isolation/security for private deployments? (SRE/priv-deploy input)
- Does lowering autoscale threshold increase churn on scale events leading to instability? Need to test with traffic replay.
- Can we expand pre-warming for large-model KV caches so scaling is less painful? (serving-runtime)

Testing / validation plan (quick bullets to propose):
- Run two staged traffic replays in staging: (a) 3x normal spike over 1h, (b) 6x short burst repeated — measure scaling latency and tail QPS impact. Owner: Javier. Target: 2026-03-20.
- Load-test autoscale change in canary region with small fleet (50 GPUs) and watch queueing and OOMs. Owner: Samir. Target: 2026-03-24.
- Finance: model cost impact of committing +120 GPUs vs using on-demand for observed spike profile. Owner: Emma. Deliverable: small spreadsheet with blended unit costs and break-even point. Target: 2026-03-19.

Proposed agenda for 30-minute sync:
- 0:00–0:05 quick data recap (me)
- 0:05–0:12 proposal + rationale for +120 GPUs (Samir + me)
- 0:12–0:20 autoscale threshold change (tradeoffs + test plan)
- 0:20–0:25 burst pool design + ownership
- 0:25–0:30 action items and owners (confirm owners + deadlines)

Action items (capture during/after meeting):
- [ ] Samir: finalize autoscale test harness and schedule traffic replay (due 2026-03-18).
- [ ] Emma: run cost sensitivity analysis for +120 commit vs on-demand (due 2026-03-19).
- [ ] Javier: prototype burst pool allocation logic and permissions doc (due 2026-03-22).
- [ ] Claire: update Confluence playbook with proposed thresholds and link to PR/benchmarks (due 2026-03-21).

Notes / talking points to remember:
- Emphasize predictability for enterprise customers — they prefer reserved capacity even if slightly higher cost.
- Highlight that 90% threshold is about reducing tail latency incidents, not about increasing spend.
- If finance pushes back on commit, propose a hybrid: commit +60 GPUs now, revisit in 45 days.

Side ideas / experiments to bring up if we have time:
- Spot/short-lived reservations for non-prod workloads to free up capacity for prod spikes.
- Pricing incentive for customers to shift heavy batch jobs to off-peak windows (we can offer cheaper queue slots).
- Auto-suggest reservation recommendations in Console based on a customer's 90-day trailing usage (tie to Optimize product).

Stash of related tickets / links (quick):
- MLINFR-1234 (autoscale metrics dashboard)
- MLINFR-1302 (burst-pool design RFC)
- PR: serving-runtime #738 (scale-up perf improvement)
- Confluence: GPU Capacity Playbook (section: reservation-sizing)

Personal notes / reminders to self:
- Keep language simple for exec summary if Emma wants a short note to present to Finance.
- Bring up telemetry gap around model-specific memory anomalies (might skew utilization).
- Ask SRE to add a 'spike' tag to incident reports so we can correlate real incidents with our simulated spikes.

End of scratchpad. Will tidy up and convert action checklist into a shared Asana/Linear board after the meeting.
